meaning: One of the separate resources inside a computer that a workload can run out of, such as the front end or back end of a CPU core, memory bandwidth, a GPU engine, storage or the network. When one resource is fully used, the others sit partly idle.
A resource saturates when the work asks it for as much per second as it can deliver. After that point, the job cannot go faster on that machine.
The part of a CPU core that fetches instructions and decodes them.
The part of a CPU core that executes the decoded instructions on its arithmetic units.
The rate at which memory can deliver data to a core, measured in GB/s.
The time one fetch from memory takes, measured in nanoseconds. It becomes the limit when each address depends on the value fetched before it.
GPU units that execute matrix multiply-and-accumulate instructions, which is the arithmetic that neural networks run on.
The integer and floating-point units of a GPU that run ordinary GPU code, such as batched physics.
The core processing unit of an NVIDIA GPU. A card has many SMs, and SM activity is the fraction of time they had work.
GPU hardware that speeds up the search for which triangle a ray hits.
The fixed-function engine on a GPU that compresses frames into video.
The fixed-function engine on a GPU that turns video back into frames.
NVIDIA's tool for monitoring a fleet of GPUs. It reports separate fields for each GPU resource, such as SM activity, tensor activity and memory activity.
In nvidia-smi, the percentage of time during which at least one GPU program was executing. It does not say how much of the card that program used.
A program that runs on the GPU.
The EC2 network device that moves data over ordinary IP networking.
The EC2 network device that bypasses the operating system so that many machines can train one model together.
The network disk of an EC2 instance. The instance type sets its maximum throughput.
The unit in which EC2 counts processor capacity. On most instance sizes, two vCPUs are one physical core.
The video codec that LeRobot writes by default.
A small imitation-learning policy that predicts a chunk of future actions at once.
A policy built on a vision-language model. It takes images and text as input and outputs robot actions.
A portable file format for trained networks.
NVIDIA's inference compiler. It turns a trained network into an engine tuned for one GPU type.
A compiled version of a network, tuned for one GPU type and built on the target device.
The set of event counters built into a processor.
A model's own compact summary of a frame, stored as a vector of numbers.
The corrections to a model's weights that a training step computes. In multi-node training, every node exchanges them with the others at every step.

A group of jobs that share the same three properties: duration, coupling and interruptibility. The five workload types are Independent tasks, Long single-machine runs, Multi-node training, Always-on streams and Real-time on the robot. The workload type tells you which scheduler and purchase option fit a job.
How long one unit of a job's work runs.
Whether the pieces of a job exchange data while they run, so that each piece needs the others to be running at the same moment.
Whether a job can lose its machine and resume, losing no more than one unit of work.
A small test program that is measured in place of the real one, such as a MuJoCo humanoid in place of the arm, or matrix-vector products in place of a policy.
One kind of job that the robot's loop hands to a computer, such as decoding video or stepping a simulation.
One of the six steps that the arm's data passes through: collect, curate, simulate, train, evaluate and deploy.
NVIDIA's desk-side computer, whose CPU and GPU share one memory. It is one of the two machines we measured.
NVIDIA's small robot computer. It is the other machine we measured.
A small benchmark task in simulation, in which a controller balances a pole on a cart.
NVIDIA's toolkit for curating training data for physical AI.
A service that queues jobs and starts machines for them, such as AWS Batch, AWS Parallel Computing Service, Amazon SageMaker HyperPod or Amazon EKS.
To vary a training image, for example with a crop or a colour shift, so that the policy sees more variety.
